modules.title: Crystal fields, orbitals and the Jahn–Teller effect
modules.summary: Connect point-group representations to d-orbital levels, tetragonal fields, spin–orbit coupling, and an analytically solvable electron–distortion model.

lessons.title: split from d-orbital shape to crystal field
lessons.summary: Using the same set of real spherical harmonic coordinates, understand how the five orbitals are grouped by point group and what exactly the splitting parameters represent.

sections.title: five orbitals and ten single electron states
sections.text: Choose five normalized real d spherical harmonics xy, yz, xz, x²−y² and 3z²−r², each with ↑ and ↓. The ten-dimensional matrix describes ten single-electron basis states, not ten electrons automatically present in the system. Orbital colors show signs of real basis functions; radius illustrates angular distributions without an actual atomic radial scale.
sections.formula: d orbital space dimension 2l+1=5; single electron dimension of d⊗spin 5×2=10

sections.title: Two sets of energy of the octahedron maintain the center of gravity
sections.text: In ideal Oh coordination, xy,yz,xz form t₂g and the other two orbitals form e_g. Define Δ=E(e_g)−E(t₂g)>0 and place the five-orbital energy barycenter at zero to fix both sets of energies. Changing Δ changes energies only, not ligand bond lengths automatically.

sections.title: Tetrahedra order and label
sections.text: ideal Td context, the double e is lower than the triple t₂. Td has no inversion and no g/u is added to the label. The Δ entered here is the positive splitting amount of the current geometry; the same value is not treated as a coordination conversion of the same real material, nor is the empirical ratio between octahedron and tetrahedron automatically applied.

sections.title: The difference between material background and model
sections.text: NiO is the material background for learning the localized octahedron crystal field , but the d⁸ problem of Ni²⁺ also requires information on interactions between electrons, Hund multiplet and other information. This experiment does not have these terms, so it only shows the single-electron symmetry and the given energy level parameters. The high and low spin or ground state of the real material cannot be announced by the energy level diagram alone.
sections.formula: single-electron crystal field spectrum ≠ multi-electron multiplet spectrum ≠ material magnetic ground state prediction

lessons.title: tetragonal crystal field , SOC and degenerate subspaces
lessons.summary: goes from explicit Ds/Dt level parameters into full L·S coupling, distinguishing repeatable subspace information from arbitrary eigenbases.

sections.title: Ds and Dt are energy level parameters
sections.text: Here tetragonal terms act on the five d orbitals with specified diagonal coefficients, and Δ=10Dq for Oh. Ds/Dt are not fitted from ligand coordinates; their signs cannot be called elongation or compression independently of the convention. The 3D ligands still show an ideal background. Connecting distortions requires a separate mapping from displacements to crystal-field parameters.

sections.title: SOC mixes states throughout the full ten-dimensional space
sections.text: Angular-momentum matrices are transformed from l=2 raising/lowering operators into the real-orbital basis used by the 3D plot. L and S use units of ℏ, and λ uses eV. At zero crystal field, j=l±s gives an independently checkable analytical limit. Negative λ reverses the two level-group orderings without changing matrix or angular-momentum conventions.
sections.formula: H=H_CF⊗I₂+λL·S; E_j=λ[j(j+1)−l(l+1)−s(s+1)]/2; j=3/2:−3λ/2（4 state), j=5/2:λ（6 state)

sections.title: Kramers Pairing and stable angular density
sections.text: This model has no external magnetic field or other time reversal breaking terms, and the spin 1/2 enable level is at least Kramers pairs. A single eigenvector in a degenerate subspace can be arbitrary change of basis , so the main graph shows the angular density averaged over that subspace, traced over the spins. It is invariant under change of basis inside the subspace; the sum of the orbital projection weights is 1, not the multi-electron occupation number.

lessons.title: E⊗e: Distorted potential energy surface obtained from electron splitting
lessons.summary: Use an independent doublet model to derive two adiabatic potential energy surfaces, minimum radius and stabilization energy, and understand the extent of the circular valley.

sections.title: First indicate the two electronic states and two coordinates
sections.text: This section independently takes the two-fold electron basis [z²,x²−y²] and the two dimensionless reduced coordinates Q₂ and Q₃. The linear coupling is specified by a real coefficient g, and the elastic coefficient K must be positive. The ten-dimensional SOC matrix in the previous section is not automatically cut into two dimensions here, nor is Q converted into actual atomic displacement.

sections.title: obtains two potential energy surfaces after diagonalization
sections.text: Electronic eigenvalues are ±|g|ρ, where ρ is the radius in the two-dimensional coordinate space. Adding elastic energy gives upper and lower adiabatic surfaces. For g≠0, the origin is a conical intersection; its lower state is not unique, so an arbitrary numerical eigenvector has no unique orbital interpretation.

sections.title: The minimum value comes from the analytical derivative
sections.text: The lower surface’s radial derivative is Kρ−|g|, so its minimum radius is |g|/K and its energy lies g²/(2K) below the origin. The program reports this analytical global minimum even outside the current 2D window, and the radial curve includes that radius. At g=0, the origin is the only minimum.

sections.title: A circular valley is not a continuous rotational symmetry of an actual crystal
sections.text: linear model only relies on ρ, so the minimum set is a circle when g≠0. This is an accidental continuous degeneracy of the model; higher-order couplings and environmental anisotropy can choose discrete directions. The current calculation does not include nuclear kinetic energy, zero-point vibrations, dynamic JT tunneling, temperature, or multiple electron occupancy; it provides a mechanistic example of structural distortion classroom rather than a real material phase diagram.
sections.formula: Radial curvature K>0; round valley tangential curvature is 0 (only this linear adiabatic model)

exercises.title: Deduced from the center of gravity constraint crystal field energy level
exercises.prompt: only considers single electron d orbitals, no SOC and no tetragonal terms, and takes the positive splitting amount Δ=1 eV.

steps.prompt: What two groups are the five d orbitals divided into in Oh?
steps.hint: Count xy, yz, xz and the remaining two orbits.
steps.explanation: t₂g includes xy, yz, xz, e_g includes x²−y² and 3z²−r², and the total dimension is 3+2=5.

steps.prompt: What are the correct conditions for taking the center of gravity of orbital energy to zero?
steps.hint: Weight the energy barycenter by orbital multiplicities.
steps.explanation: triple t₂g and double e_g each contribute 3E_t and 2E_e.

steps.prompt: Using E_e−E_t=1 as well, what are the two energies?
steps.explanation: E_t=−2/5 eV and E_e=3/5 eV: the separation is 1 and the orbital energy barycenter is zero.

steps.prompt: For ideal Td with a positive splitting of 1 eV, which statement is correct?
choices: low e is −0.6, high t₂ is 0.4, no g is added to the label
low t₂g is −0.4, high e_g is 0.6
Only the number of orbitals can change, not their ordering
steps.hint: The doublet lies lower in Td, which has no inversion.
steps.explanation: 2(−0.6)+3(0.4)=0; e/t₂ tag of Td has no g/u. This parameter comparison is not a quantitative prediction of true coordination transitions.

exercises.title: Analytical SOC limit and Kramers pairs
exercises.prompt: Let crystal field Δ, Ds, and Dt be all 0, and take l=2, s=1/2, and λ=0.2 eV.

steps.prompt: Which two j are allowed for angular momentum coupling?
steps.hint: has a single electron spin of 1/2, j=l±s.
steps.explanation: l=2 is coupled with s=1/2 to obtain j=3/2, 5/2, corresponding to 4 and 6 states.

steps.prompt: For j=3/2, what are the L·S eigenvalue and energy?
steps.explanation: (15/4−6−3/4)/2=−3/2, multiply by λ to get −0.3 eV; the other six states are +0.2 eV.

steps.prompt: After changing λ to −0.2 eV, which group is lower?
choices: The two groups must still be degenerate
steps.hint: All SOC eigenvalues change sign with λ.
steps.explanation: j=5/2 energy is λ=−0.2 eV; j=3/2 is −3λ/2=+0.3 eV.

steps.prompt: With a crystal field but no magnetic field, which graphical interpretation is most reliable?
choices: The shape of any single degenerate eigenvector is unique
The group-averaged angular density is invariant under a change of basis within the degenerate subspace; the levels retain Kramers pairing.
10 ground states means there are 10 electrons
steps.hint: distinguishes between N-dimensional single electron basis and electron number, and uses T²=−1.
steps.explanation: time reversal Keep Kramers pairwise degenerate, and average after projection to the entire group to avoid mistaking any eigenbase selection for physical differences.

exercises.title: hand calculation of round valley and stabilization energy of E⊗e
exercises.prompt: Take g=1 eV, K=2 eV, Q₂, Q₃ as dimensionless coordinates; here only the adiabatic potential energy surface is obtained.

steps.prompt: What are the two eigenvalues ​​of the electron matrix g(Q₂τx+Q₃τz)?
steps.hint: The square of the matrix is ​​g²(Q₂²+Q₃²)I.
steps.explanation: Define ρ=√(Q₂²+Q₃²), the electron energy is ±|g|ρ, and add the same Kρ²/2.

steps.prompt: What is the minimum radius of the lower potential energy surface V−=ρ²−ρ?
steps.explanation: ρ₀=|g|/K=1/2. The radial second derivative is K=2>0.

steps.prompt: What are the minimum energy and the positive stabilization energy?
steps.explanation: V_min=−g²/(2K)=−1/4 eV, the energy is reduced by 1/4 eV relative to the origin.

steps.prompt: What is the most accurate conclusion about equal energy in all directions of the same radius?
choices: A real crystal must have continuous spatial rotation symmetry
You must choose a direction at random, which is called the only ground state.
The linear model has an accidental circular valley; higher-order terms can select discrete directions
steps.hint: Only ρ appears in potential energy, not azimuth .
steps.explanation: The round valley belongs to this truncated model; without nuclear kinetic energy, tunneling or higher-order coupling, it cannot be regarded as equivalent to the full structural and dynamic conclusions of real materials.

cases.title: NiO background: localized octahedrons and multi-electron boundaries
cases.summary: Connect the existing NiO structure and magnetic material cases to the local d orbital grouping to distinguish the single electron crystal field diagram from d⁸ multiplet .
cases.kind: Real material coordination background + single electron teaching model
cases.assumption: The d⁸ multi-electron interaction of Ni²⁺ is not in this 10×10 single electron model; the parameters are original teaching values ​​and do not predict NiO high and low spin, magnetic ground state or measured d–d excitation.

cases.title: Ideal tetrahedral cluster: changing coordination, not changing coordinate convention
cases.summary: Compare the ideal background of four equidistant ligands to six equidistant ligands and observe the e/t₂ ordering and d-orbital angle distribution.
cases.assumption: The real compound is not specified, and the potential energy is not recalculated from the ligand position; Δ, Ds, Dt, and λ are all given parameters, and the ligand bond length remains in the visual unit 1.

cases.title: Jahn–Teller mechanism: electron energy and distortion cost
cases.summary: Use analysis E⊗e Tsuburaya to understand how electron splitting compensates for elastic energy, and connect to existing structural distortion and Landau classes.
cases.assumption: Q₂/Q₃ is a dimensionless reduced coordinate; it is not an automatically generated standard crystal model, nor is it g/K fitted from the real structure. Does not include nuclear kinetic energy, dynamic JT, SOC, or phase transition temperature.
